transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just can't seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. I work at a freight warehouse, and lately, every little thing pulls me off my count. A beeper goes off, or the forklift alarm starts blaring... you know, they actually just got these new electric forklifts, and the backup alarm on them is this awful, high-pitched screech. It's not a normal beep like the old propane ones we used to have. I told my supervisor, Gary, that it's terrible, but he never listens. He’s been like that since we were at the old facility on 4th street. 

But anyway... where was I? Oh, right, so someone moves a pallet or that awful alarm goes off, and my focus is just completely gone. Then I look down and realize I've put entirely the wrong numbers into the inventory system.
Are you having trouble focusing or getting distracted at home or in your free time as well?

At home? Um, I haven't really noticed it as much there. I mean, my free time is mostly just me trying to keep the house in order or watching a little TV. I was trying to watch that new baking competition show the other night. They make these giant sculptures out of chocolate. It's amazing how they get it to not melt under all those studio lights. I actually took a culinary class back when I was taking a few courses at the community college years ago, and tempering chocolate is so hard. You have to get the temperature exactly right on the thermometer or it gets all dull and streaky when it dries. My instructor was so strict about it, he'd make us throw the whole batch out and start over if it wasn't perfectly shiny. 

But, um... what was I saying? Oh, right, my free time. No, I don't think I'm having trouble focusing at the house, really. I just haven't noticed it happening there. Mostly just at work with all that noise.
Are you feeling overwhelmed or stressed by your difficulty focusing at work?

Overwhelmed? Yeah, I guess I am. It's just embarrassing, honestly, because I’ve had to start going to my supervisor to double-check everything after making those inventory errors. And Gary, he's just... well, he's always eating those little peppermint candies, you know? The ones with the red stripes wrapped in the crinkly plastic. And he crunches them. Who crunches a hard mint? You're supposed to let them dissolve. It makes this awful sound right in my ear while he's looking over my clipboard. I used to buy these really nice honey lozenges from the farmer's market on weekends, the ones made by that local beekeeper... oh, what was his name? Arthur, maybe? Anyway, they were so much better for your throat, and they didn't crack your teeth. 

But, um, what were we talking about? Oh, the stress from work. Yeah, it's just a lot right now. And it bleeds into things at home, too. My husband and I have been arguing enough lately that it feels like we’re just walking around each other, trying not to step on each other's toes. It's really not how things were supposed to go. He just retired, and we were supposed to be settling into his retirement, you know? Taking it easy. We had all these plans to maybe rent an RV and drive down to Florida. My sister lives near Clearwater, right by that aquarium with the rescue dolphins. I think they made a movie about one of them... the one with the plastic tail? I can't remember the name of it.
Do you find that you're having trouble remembering things that you would normally be able to recall?

Memory? No, I don't think so. My memory is actually pretty sharp, usually. I just remembered to send a card for my niece's birthday last week on time, actually. She just turned twelve, and they grow up so fast. We got her this little kit to make her own jewelry, with all these tiny glass beads. They were so pretty, all iridescent and shiny, kind of like sea glass. Have you ever been down to the beach and looked for sea glass? We used to go to this spot up the coast when I was taking classes at the community college, just walking for hours looking for the blue ones. The blue ones are the rarest because they come from old medicine bottles, mostly. People used to just throw their trash right into the ocean, which is terrible to think about now, but the glass gets all smooth and frosted from the sand and the waves. I had a whole mason jar full of it on my windowsill in my old apartment... 

But, um, wait, what were you asking me? Oh, right, my memory. No, I haven't had any trouble remembering things. It's really just the focusing at the warehouse that's getting to me.
Do you feel anxious or worried when you're at work and having trouble focusing?

Anxious? I mean, a little bit, sure. It's just frustrating, you know? Like I'm messing up things I've done a thousand times. And the warehouse is just so huge and echoey. They just painted the floors this really bright, glossy gray, too. Supposedly it's to help the forklifts grip better or something, but it reflects the overhead lights right into your eyes. It reminds me of this roller rink I used to go to when I was a teenager. They had these gray floors and they'd play disco music... they had this huge mirrored ball in the center. We used to go every Friday night. I had these white skates with bright pink pom-poms on the laces. My mom hated those pom-poms because they'd get dirty so fast, and she'd try to wash them in the sink with dish soap, but they never really looked the same after they got wet...

Um, what was I saying? Oh, right, work. Yeah, I guess it makes me a little anxious when I can't concentrate. But mostly it's just annoying.
Do you find that your emotions change quickly or intensely in response to small things at work?

Emotions changing? Well, it's kind of a mix, honestly. Some days I wake up and I just feel... almost too upbeat, you know? Like I have all this energy. I feel like I could reorganize the entire warehouse inventory by myself, and then come home and fix up the whole house before dinner. I actually started repainting the guest bedroom last week because I just felt so motivated. I picked out this color, it's called "Morning Dew," and it's this really soft, pale green. It reminds me of the color of the leaves on the willow tree we had in my backyard growing up. My dad planted it when I was born, and it got so huge. We used to sit under it in the summer and eat watermelon, and my brother would always try to spit the seeds the farthest. He actually chipped a tooth once because he tripped over one of the roots while he was running away from a bee...

Oh, but you were asking about my emotions at work. Right. Well, it's not just work. It's like, I have all these big plans, and I feel great about them, but then if someone—like my husband—questions even one little thing about what I'm doing, I just snap at him. Over the smallest things, too. Like, he asked why I bought three gallons of that green paint instead of two, and I just lost it on him. It's like this switch flips and I just get so irritated so fast.
Do you find that these intense emotional shifts happen throughout the day or are they more limited to specific times or situations?

Well, it's not really about the time of day, I don't think. It's just like I was saying, some days I wake up and I feel almost too upbeat, like I have the energy to fix the whole house and reorganize the entire warehouse before dinner. I just feel so capable, you know? Like nothing can stop me. I even bought all those extra gallons of paint because I figured, why stop at the guest room? I could do the hallway, too. The hallway hasn't been painted since we moved in, and it's this awful beige color. Beige is just so depressing, don't you think? It reminds me of the waiting room at my dentist's office. He has these terrible fluorescent lights and this beige wallpaper with tiny little brown flowers on it. I always stare at it when I'm getting my teeth cleaned. The hygienist there, she has the heaviest hands. My gums always ache for two days after I go... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, the emotional shifts. Right. Yeah, so I'll be feeling fantastic, ready to conquer the world, and then my husband will just ask one little question about my plans, and I just snap at him. It doesn't matter if it's morning or night, if he questions me over something small, I just lose my temper instantly.
Do you think your emotional shifts, like snapping at your husband, happen more often on days when you're having a lot of trouble focusing at work?

Focusing at work... hmm, I don't know if they're connected like that. Honestly, I haven't really paid attention to whether one happens on the same day as the other. Work is just work, you know? Sometimes the forklifts are acting up, or the scanner guns won't connect to the Wi-Fi. Those scanners are the absolute worst. They updated the software last month, and supposedly it was going to make scanning barcodes twice as fast, but half the time the screen just freezes and you have to pop the battery out to restart it. And the batteries are held in by this tiny little plastic clip that always feels like it's going to snap right off if you push it too hard. My coworker, Dave, he actually broke one of the clips last week, and the supervisor got so mad. Dave's a good guy, though. He brings in donuts every other Friday from this little bakery near his house. They make these maple bars that are just incredible, like, the frosting is so thick and sweet. I always try to get one before they're gone, but you have to be quick because the guys on the early shift usually wipe them out by 9 AM...

Anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, the snapping at my husband. Yeah, I'm not really sure if it happens more on days when I can't focus. I haven't really noticed a pattern like that.
Do you think your trouble focusing at work is affecting your relationship with your husband?

Well, I don't know if the focusing at work is directly causing the issues with him, but... things are definitely tense. Like, at work, I've had to go back and double-check things with my supervisor because I keep making these stupid inventory errors. It's so frustrating because I've been doing this job for years, and normally I can just breeze through the aisles. But lately, I'll put a pallet of the wrong size bolts in section C, and then someone else has to go find it. The bolts they buy now are so cheap anyway. The threads strip if you look at them funny. My husband bought a box of them last month to fix the hinges on the back gate, and he went through half the box just trying to get three good ones to catch. The gate still sags a little bit on the left side, which drives me crazy when I'm trying to pull the lawnmower out...

Oh, right, my husband. Yeah, at home, we've just been arguing so much lately. It's gotten to the point where it feels like we're just walking around each other, trying not to step on any landmines, you know? He just retired, and this was supposed to be this nice time for us to settle into his retirement, maybe do some traveling, but instead we're just bickering. We were supposed to go to Mount Rushmore this summer. Have you ever been? I hear the faces are actually a lot smaller in person than you'd expect from the pictures... but anyway, yeah, the arguing is definitely putting a damper on his retirement.
Do you think the days when you have a lot of trouble focusing at work are also the days when you're more likely to snap at your husband?

I think you might have asked me that a minute ago, right? About the work days and the snapping. I really still don't know if they happen on the exact same days. I just haven't kept a record of it or anything. Keeping track of things is getting harder anyway, to be honest. Like my calendar at home, it's one of those big ones with the Thomas Kinkade paintings for every month. My sister gets me one every Christmas without fail. She loves those little cottages with the glowing windows. She actually has a whole collection of the collector plates in her dining room. They collect so much dust, though. I keep telling her she needs to get a glass cabinet for them, but she insists on having them out on these little wire stands. One time her cat, Barnaby—he's this huge orange tabby, he has to weigh at least eighteen pounds—he jumped right up on the buffet and knocked two of them onto the floor. Shattered everywhere. It took us an hour to vacuum up all the pieces because her rug is this really busy floral pattern and you couldn't see the white ceramic bits... 

But anyway, what were we just saying? Oh, right, the days at work. Yeah, like I said, I really couldn't tell you if they line up with when I get mad at my husband. I just haven't paid that much attention to the exact timing of it all.
Do you think there's a direct connection between the days you have a lot of trouble focusing at work and the days you experience these intense emotional shifts?

I feel like we keep going in circles with this, Doc. You keep asking if the work stuff and the emotional stuff are connected, and I really, honestly don't know. I haven't noticed a direct connection. I'm not keeping a journal or anything. A journal might be nice, actually. My niece bought me one of those fancy bullet journals last year for my birthday. It has these really thick, dotted pages and a little ribbon marker. She said it's supposed to help with organization and mindfulness, whatever that means. She's really into all that wellness stuff now, drinking matcha lattes and going to hot yoga. I tried hot yoga once with her, and I thought I was going to pass out. It was like 105 degrees in that room, and everyone was just dripping sweat onto their mats. It smelled like old gym socks and lavender essential oil. And the instructor kept telling us to "breathe into our tight spaces," which just sounded ridiculous when I was trying not to slide right off my own arms in a downward dog... 

But yeah, I don't know. I just haven't noticed if the focusing and the emotional shifts happen on the exact same days. It's just a lot going on all at once.
Do you think your trouble focusing at work contributes to your intense emotional shifts?

Doc, are you even listening to me? I feel like you've asked me the exact same thing four times now just using slightly different words. I really, truly don't know if the work focusing and the emotional stuff are connected. I just don't. It's all just a big jumble right now. 

Speaking of jumbles, you should see the back of my car. I've been meaning to clean it out for weeks, but I just keep tossing things back there. There's an umbrella, three reusable grocery bags, a pair of boots I meant to return to the shoe store in the mall... Oh, the mall is just so depressing these days, isn't it? Half the stores are boarded up, and the ones that are open always seem to be having going-out-of-business sales. I went in there last week to get a pretzel—you know, the big soft ones with the salt and the cheese dip? But even the pretzel stand was closed! Just a handwritten sign saying "Closed for maintenance." What kind of maintenance does a pretzel stand need? It's just a warmer and a cash register. I ended up getting a coffee from the food court instead, but it tasted burnt. I think they just leave the pots sitting on the burner all day. 

Anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. No, I don't know if the work stuff makes the emotional stuff happen. I really don't have an answer for you on that one.
Do you have difficulty focusing during tasks that require sustained mental effort outside of work?

Outside of work? I mean, I guess it depends on what you mean by sustained mental effort. Like, I don't really know if I have trouble with that kind of thing. I haven't really thought about it. I mean, I do crossword puzzles sometimes, usually the ones in the Sunday paper. Well, not the New York Times one, that one is impossible. I stick to the local paper. My husband usually grabs it from the driveway before I even get up, and he leaves the puzzle section on the kitchen island for me. He knows I like to do it while I have my morning coffee. 

We just got a new coffee maker, actually. One of those fancy ones that grinds the beans right before it brews. It's so loud, though! The first time we used it, I thought a jet engine was taking off in the kitchen. It scared our dog half to death. He's a little terrier mix, Buster, and he's already so skittish. He spent the rest of the morning hiding under the sofa. We had to coax him out with a piece of cheese. He loves sharp cheddar, but you have to be careful not to give him too much or it upsets his stomach. 

But anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, focusing outside of work. Yeah, I don't really know. I just haven't paid that much attention to it, to be honest.
Do you have trouble concentrating on things you enjoy doing in your free time?

Things I enjoy? I don't know, I haven't really noticed if I have trouble concentrating on them. I mean, I guess it depends on the day. I used to really like knitting. I made this beautiful afghan for my sister a few years ago. It took me months. It was this gorgeous teal color, like the ocean on a really clear day. We went to the beach last summer, actually, down to the Cape. It rained for three days straight. We were stuck in this tiny little rental cottage that smelled like mildew and stale popcorn. My husband tried to make the best of it and bought a 1000-piece jigsaw puzzle of a lighthouse. We spent hours hunched over that tiny coffee table, trying to find all the edge pieces. I think we were missing a corner piece, which drove him absolutely crazy. He gets so fixated on things like that. He spent an hour crawling around on the floor with a flashlight looking for it. Turns out Buster had chewed it up. Found it under the sofa, covered in dog spit. 

But anyway, what was the question? Oh, concentrating on fun stuff. Yeah, I'm really not sure. I haven't really paid attention to whether I'm struggling with that or not.
Do you have difficulty concentrating when you're doing something you enjoy, like watching TV or reading a book?

Watching TV or reading? I... I don't know. I really don't. It's hard to say if I have trouble focusing on them because I just haven't paid attention to it. I mean, I do watch TV in the evenings sometimes. Mostly those home renovation shows. It's amazing what they can do with a little paint and some new countertops, isn't it? We've been talking about redoing our kitchen for years, but the cost is just astronomical. Have you seen the price of lumber lately? My neighbor, Gary, he's building a new deck on the back of his house, and he was telling me that a single piece of plywood is like three times what it used to be. He's a nice guy, Gary. A little loud sometimes, especially when his favorite football team is playing, but he always helps shovel our driveway in the winter. He's got one of those heavy-duty snowblowers. The bright orange kind. I think it's a Toro. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, TV and books. Yeah, I just... I don't know. I can't really give you a straight answer on that because I just haven't noticed one way or the other.
Do you find yourself getting distracted or losing interest when watching your favorite TV shows?

My favorite TV shows? Gosh, I don't really know if I lose interest. I mean, I guess I just haven't really thought about it. I watch those renovation shows, like I said. And sometimes the baking ones. The baking ones are fun, except when they make them do those crazy sculptures out of fondant. Nobody actually likes eating fondant, do they? It's just sugary playdough. My niece had a cake like that for her wedding. Beautiful cake, looked exactly like a birch tree. But it tasted like cardboard. We had the wedding out at this little farm venue she found online. The weather was perfect, not too hot, but the mosquitoes were terrible. They had these big citronella torches set up everywhere, but they didn't do a lick of good. My husband got bit right on the eyelid, swelled up like a golf ball. He had to wear his sunglasses for the rest of the reception, even when we were inside eating dinner. People probably thought he was trying to be some kind of celebrity. 

But, um... what did you ask me? Distracted during TV shows? Yeah, I just... I haven't really paid enough attention to tell you, honestly. I don't know.
Do you find it hard to focus on tasks like cooking or cleaning at home?

Cooking or cleaning? I... well, I don't really know. I just haven't paid enough attention to see if I'm having trouble focusing on them. I do try to keep the house tidy, you know. I was actually just cleaning out the hall closet the other day. It was a complete disaster area. We had all these old winter coats shoved in there, and half of them don't even fit anymore. I found my husband's old down jacket from when he worked at the warehouse. He used to drive a forklift there, years ago. Long shifts, sometimes twelve hours a day. He’d come home smelling like exhaust and cardboard. They had this one supervisor, a guy named Rick, who used to make them work through their breaks if a shipment was late. Rick drove this beat-up old Mustang, thought he was the coolest guy in town. It broke down in the parking lot once, and my husband had to help him jump-start it in the pouring rain. He ruined a good pair of work boots that day. 

Anyway, what was it you were asking? Focusing on chores? Yeah, I'm really not sure. I just haven't noticed if it's hard for me or not.
Do you have trouble concentrating when doing something that requires you to think carefully for a long time, like working on a puzzle?

Puzzles? Oh, um... I don't know. I really couldn't tell you. I haven't tried to do a puzzle in... gosh, I don't even know how long. I just haven't paid attention to whether I can focus on things like that. My sister, Brenda, she loves those big thousand-piece puzzles. The ones with the landscapes or the little European villages. She glues them together when she's done and frames them. Her whole hallway is covered in them. It looks like a museum in there. She gets them from this little hobby shop downtown. The owner there, Mr. Henderson, he's been running that place since we were kids. He used to sell these little balsa wood airplanes that you'd wind up with a rubber band. We'd fly them in the park until they got stuck in the oak trees. Those trees are huge now. The city came through a few years ago and trimmed all the branches back because they were interfering with the power lines. They left this huge mess of sawdust all over the sidewalks. It took weeks for the rain to finally wash it all away. 

But, sorry, what did you ask me? Thinking carefully about things? Yeah, I just... I really don't know. I haven't noticed one way or the other.
Do you find yourself having trouble finishing things you start when you're doing something you enjoy?

Finishing things I enjoy? I... gosh, I don't really know if I have trouble with that. I just haven't really noticed one way or the other. I mean, I like fixing up old furniture when I have the time, but I don't know if I finish it any differently than I used to. I actually started sanding down this old wooden rocking chair a while back. Found it at that big flea market out on Route 9, you know the one? They always have that guy there selling the vintage license plates. My dad used to collect those. He had one from every single state nailed up on the wall in our old garage. Took him years to find a Hawaii one. That garage always smelled like motor oil and damp newspapers. We used to keep our old golden retriever, Buster, out there during thunderstorms because he’d get so scared he’d chew on the baseboards inside the house. He completely ruined the trim in the dining room once during a really bad summer storm. My mom was so mad she made my dad repaint the whole room, and he chose this awful mustard yellow color that made everyone look slightly sick when the overhead light was on... 

But, um, I'm sorry, what was the question? Finishing things I start? Yeah, I just... I really couldn't say. I haven't paid enough attention to it to give you a good answer.
Do you have difficulty concentrating on tasks outside of work, such as hobbies or personal projects?

Hobbies or personal projects? Um... I don't know. I really couldn't say if I have a hard time concentrating on them. I just haven't been keeping track of my focus like that. I do like gardening, though. I was out there pulling weeds from the tomato beds yesterday. The soil is finally getting warm enough. We had a late frost this year that nearly wiped out all the seedlings I started in the kitchen window. I usually start them in these little peat pots, the kind that just break down in the dirt. My grandmother taught me how to do that. She had this incredible garden back in Ohio. Huge beefsteak tomatoes, bigger than your fist. She used to can them all in the fall. Her cellar was lined with these dusty mason jars full of tomatoes and green beans and pickled beets. I always hated the beets. They tasted like dirt to me, but my grandfather would eat them straight out of the jar with a fork while he watched the evening news. He always watched Walter Cronkite. Never missed a broadcast. He had this old recliner that squeaked every time he leaned back...

Wait, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Concentrating on hobbies? Yeah, I just... I don't really know. I haven't noticed if it's hard or not.
